projection.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and let $k$ be an arbitrary field. On separated finite-type complex varieties, the ordinary analytic sheaf operations restrict to bounded algebraically constructible complexes $D_c^b(-;k)$ ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]): $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, the tensor/internal-Hom adjunction, coherent composition, support localization, ordinary and extraordinary proper base change, the projection formula and trace. Proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$. Verdier duality is involutive there and exchanges these adjoints. On a smooth complex $d$-fold $\omega_X=k_X[2d]$, and for a smooth map of relative dimension $d$, $f^!=f^*[2d]$. Coefficient extensions commute with these operations on bounded constructible inputs. The bounded constructibility and finite coefficient models are those of [[lem-complex-algebraic-stratifications-have-finite-conical-cochain-models]] and [[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]].
projection.strategy: Assume AC. Sources: Bernstein-Lunts, Part I SS1.4.1-SS1.4.6 (tensor-Hom, composition, adjunctions, proper equality, open localization triangles and base change) and SS1.6-SS1.7 (dualizing object, Verdier duality for continuous maps, and smooth maps of relative dimension $d$), together with the finite resolution construction of Part I SS1.9/Appendices A and the derived-category simplicial comparison; BBD, Faisceaux pervers, SS1.4.1-1.4.10 (the recollement localization triangles giving localization and gluing), as an independent treatment. Step 1: the actual compact-support adjoint and coherent six-operation suppliers construct the functors and their adjunction units/counits, not just unrelated isomorphisms; their ordinary coherent composition, Cartesian exchange, projection/trace and localization diagrams are the asserted diagrams, including proper equality $Rf_!=Rf_*$ and the smooth local-product comparisons. All vector-space and injective constructions apply over an arbitrary field; their signed cochains use only $0$ and the units $\pm1$, so no characteristic hypothesis enters. Step 2: the actual finite conical and incidence suppliers prove bounded constructibility and finite coefficient models for the stated finite collection, so the constructed operations restrict to $D_c^b$ and their finite local cochain comparisons commute with field extension; the actual support construction for compactly supported operations is used, and no infinite tensor of injective products is formed. Step 3: the oriented stratified Verdier supplier gives its evaluation isomorphism and identifies the dualizing object on a smooth complex $d$-fold with $k[2d]$ through the positive complex orientation; its adjunction construction gives duality exchange and the stated smooth extraordinary pullback $f^!=f^*[2d]$, and all these maps use the same ordinary units/counits and orientation, so their coherence is the coherence of the actual construction. The integral orientation generator maps to the nonzero unit $1\in k$ over every field, including characteristic two.

Every remaining step is a finite-dimensional or canonical comparison and is choice-free.

projection.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) and the geometric and derived-incidence suppliers of [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]]. For analytic algebraic maps on its proved bounded constructible subcategory $D_c^b(-;k)$ over a field $k$, the six operations $f^*,Rf_*,Rf_!,f^!,\otimes_k^L,R\mathcal Hom$ have their three adjunctions, composition and identity comparisons, ordinary proper and extraordinary proper base change, projection formula, support localization, dualizing transitivity and trace. The comparisons commute with Cartesian pasting, composition of maps, evaluation and trace, giving a coherent pull-push product calculus. For a locally trivial product projection $\mathrm{pr}:V\times F\to V$ with finite-type smooth fibre $F$, the actual finite product cochain model gives $R\mathrm{pr}_*\mathrm{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_kC^*(F;k)$ with its ordinary unit. Smooth base change for $Rf_*$ holds whenever a supplied factorization $f=p\circ j$ has $p$ proper and $j$ an open inclusion with the conical local models of the two listed suppliers; proper maps already satisfy it. The finite constructible models commute with extension of coefficient fields. Geometric output preservation is the exact geometric supplier, not an additional axiom.
projection.strategy: Assume AC. Sources: Verdier, expose 300, SS1.2 p. 340 (base change), SS1.5 p. 341 (composition), SS5 p. 348 (submersive maps and the projection formula for a product projection); Stacks Project, Cohomology of Sheaves SS17-SS18 (base-change map and proper base change) and SS54 (projection formula Lemma 54.2); Bernstein-Lunts, Part I SS1.8 (smooth base change and compatibility with all functors). Step 1: apply the support-and-trace lemma to the actual analytic maps; its proper-support section and injective models give ordinary exchange, the projection formula, both support-localization triangles, canonical composition, units and traces, all as section-level identities carried through the same resolution comparisons. Step 2: apply the constructible Verdier theorem to the actual finite conical/incidence models; it supplies duality, orientation and the extraordinary exchange by dualizing the canonical proper base-change map, and functoriality carries pasting and trace squares to their dual squares, while the tensor-Hom and inverse/direct-image adjunctions are the signed dg comparisons of the ordinary-operations lemma. Step 3 (product projection): tensor the finite base diagram resolution with the fibre constant-diagram resolution ([[lem-finite-simplicial-constructible-sheaves-have-a-derived-incidence-model]]); each realized term has support a product of closed cells minus deleted faces, and its intersection with a small base star times $F$ has contractible factors, so the constant-sheaf comparison [[lem-locally-contractible-metric-spaces-have-singular-constant-sheaf-cohomology]] makes it section-acyclic; applying sections gives the natural finite double complex $B|_{\mathrm{star}}\otimes C^*(F;k)$ and identifies the derived image and its unit with $B\otimes C^*(F;k)$ and $B\otimes(k\to C^*(F;k))$. For smooth base change of an open inclusion $j$, a local smooth chart is a product with a contractible ball, and the boundary-star section model becomes the old finite cochain model tensored with the ball cochains, whose augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism by an explicit contraction. If the supplied $f=p\circ j$ has $p$ proper, combine this exchange with the constructed proper base-change map for $p$; compatibility with composition identifies the composite with the canonical $f$ exchange. No compactification existence theorem is inferred: the clause applies only to the stated supplied factorization. Step 4 (coefficient extension): use the geometric supplier's finite local cellular/cochain models; scalar extension is exact on vector spaces, commutes with finite sums, cohomology and finite-dimensional duals, so ordinary inverse image, finite cochain pushforward, tensor, internal Hom and the support-defined Verdier comparisons extend termwise, and the exceptional comparison follows from $f^!=D_Xf^*D_Y$; no infinite product of injective stalks is involved.

projection.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), that $k$ has characteristic zero, and that a product $G$ of complex general linear groups acts algebraically on separated finite-type complex varieties. The coherent ordinary six-operation contract holds in the equivariant bounded constructible category $D^b_{G,c}$ of [[def-equivariant-constructible-derived-category-for-complex-algebraic-varieties]] for equivariant algebraic maps: $f^*\dashv Rf_*$, $Rf_!\dashv f^!$, $\otimes_k^L\dashv R\mathcal Hom$, composition and identity comparisons, support localization, the projection formula and trace. For a Cartesian square with $f:X\to Y$, $u:Y'\to Y$, $v:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$, the actual exchange $u^*Rf_!\simeq Rf'_!v^*$ and its dual mate $u^!Rf_*\simeq Rf'_*v^!$ obey Cartesian pasting. Proper $f$ satisfies $Rf_!=Rf_*$. The normalized dualizing object restricts to the ordinary $\omega_X$; a smooth complex $d$-dimensional $X$ has $\omega_X^G=k_X[2d]$. This is not the unnormalized quotient-stack dualizing shift.
projection.strategy: Assume AC; $k$ characteristic zero. Route: apply the ordinary coherent six operations at each finite free resolution, assemble them over the finite-resolution triples, and normalize the dualizing object by the Grassmannian resolution. Sources: Bernstein-Lunts Part I, §3.1-3.6 (construction of the functors on smooth resolutions; tensor and Hom; $f^*,f^!,f_*,f_!$; their adjunctions, base change, composition and projection/trace properties; equivariant Verdier duality; equivariant constructible sheaves) and §1.9 with Appendix A (acyclicity enabling the resolution comparisons). Step 1 (operations): at each smooth free resolution use the ordinary constructed operations of [[lem-analytic-constructible-sheaves-admit-coherent-six-operations]] and [[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]]; smooth base-change comparison gives compatible transition isomorphisms, and the finite-resolution triples of [[lem-cartesian-simplicial-sheaves-model-equivariant-constructible-derived-hom]] assemble actual equivariant operations rather than unrelated isomorphisms. Adjunctions and the coherent projection/exchange/trace maps use the ordinary units and counits; their triangle and pasting identities hold at one sufficiently large finite resolution for all objects in the finite diagram and transfer through the fully faithful comparison, so Cartesian pasting and composition are preserved. Step 2 (normalization): at the Stiefel resolution $P_N\to X_N$ with base $B_N$ the normalized dualizing object is $\omega_{X_N}\otimes a_{X_N}^*\omega_{B_N}^{-1}$, correcting ordinary Verdier duality by $-2\dim_{\mathbb C}B_N$; its restriction to $X$ is the ordinary $\omega_X$, and complex orientation identifies it with $k[2\dim_{\mathbb C}X]$ when $X$ is smooth, with no group-dimension shift. Biduality, the two dual exchange identities, proper equality and the coherent unit/counit laws follow from the ordinary supplier [[thm-verdier-duality-on-oriented-stratified-complex-varieties]] together with the equivariant duality construction of the source. This is the unnormalized-quotient-stack shift exclusion recorded in the design. [AC as declared]

The comparison and normalization arguments are otherwise canonical.

projection.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the supplied injective-resolution six-functor construction. Let $f:Y\to X$ be a proper surjective morphism of finite-type complex algebraic varieties, and let $F\in D^b_c(X;k)$ for a field $k$. Write $Y_p=Y\times_X\cdots\times_XY$ with $p+1$ factors, $f_p:Y_p\to X$, and $F_p=f_p^*F$. In the analytic topology of [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]] the natural augmented derived Cech map is a quasi-isomorphism: $$F\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}Rf_{p*}F_p.$$ Here totalization is the normalized or unnormalized alternating-face total supplied by the simplicial-derived construction. There is one fixed lower cochain bound; consequently its diagonals are finite in every degree. The claim commutes with arbitrary algebraic base change and coefficient morphisms. In particular $R\Gamma(X,F)\simeq\operatorname{Tot}_pR\Gamma(Y_p,F_p)$. Individual fibers of $f$ need not be cohomologically acyclic, connected, or smooth.
projection.strategy: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Sources: Dugger-Hollander-Isaksen Appendix A (proper Cech descent by stalk contraction; PDF pp. 35-36, read in full) and Stacks Project, Hypercoverings, Lemma 3.9 and Lemmas 4.2-4.5 (general-site cohomological descent; PDF pp. 5-10, read in full). [F1] The coherent six-operation contract over an arbitrary coefficient field for analytic algebraic maps on bounded constructible complexes is [[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]]: it gives exact inverse image, ordinary proper base change, its naturality for all Cech faces and degeneracies, and the identification of $f_p^*F$ restricted to a geometric fiber with the constant pullback of $F_x$. The coefficient category is [[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]], and the restriction of the operations to it over every field, with each pulled coefficient again bounded below, is [[lem-analytic-constructible-sheaves-admit-coherent-six-operations]]. [F2] [[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]] supplies the functorial simplicial-derived total model with a uniform internal lower bound and finite-degree truncations; its local-section descent conclusion is not used as proper descent. [F3] [[thm-bounded-filtered-complex-spectral-sequence-abuts-to-filtered-homology]] gives convergence for degreewise finite filtrations, with cohomological reindexing. [A1] AC is inherited only by the supplied resolution construction; selecting one point for the stalk argument requires only a single nonempty-set selection, not a simultaneously chosen family of sections. Step 1.1 (bounded model and finite diagonals). Choose a lower bound $a$ for the cochain model of $F$; exact pullback preserves it and right-derived pushforward gives a functorial double model in degrees $p\geq0$, $q\geq a$, so in total degree $m$ there are only $0\leq p\leq m-a$ terms. Take the cone of the augmented map and filter by $p$, still bounded below after placing the augmentation in column $p=-1$. Stalks commute with its finite pieces, so by the finite-filtration spectral sequence of [F3] it suffices to prove exactness of every augmented horizontal stalk row after taking internal cohomology. Step 2.1 (stalk rows and one chosen point). Fix $x\in X$ and put $K=F_x$; surjectivity gives a nonempty proper fiber $S=Y_x$, and proper base change identifies the augmented horizontal row in internal degree $q$ with $H^q(K)\to H^q(S,K)\to H^q(S^2,K)\to\cdots$, where $K$ on each $S^{p+1}$ is its constant derived pullback from the point; [F1] intertwines all deletion and repetition maps. Pick one point $y\in S$; for $p\geq1$ let $j_p:S^p\to S^{p+1}$ insert $y$ as first coordinate and let $j_0:\mathrm{pt}\to S$ be this point. Pullback gives maps $h_p=j_p^*:H^q(S^{p+1},K)\to H^q(S^p,K)$, with $h_0$ landing in $H^q(K)$. No assertion that any positive cohomology group of $S$ vanishes is made. Step 3.1 (explicit contraction). If $d_i:S^{p+2}\to S^{p+1}$ deletes coordinate $i$, the insertion identities are $d_0j_{p+1}=\operatorname{id}$ and $d_ij_{p+1}=j_pd_{i-1}$ for $i>0$. On the augmented row put $\delta_p=\sum_{i=0}^{p+1}(-1)^id_i^*$ and let $\delta_{-1}:H^q(K)\to H^q(S,K)$ be constant pullback. The displayed identities give $h_{p+1}\delta_p+\delta_{p-1}h_p=\operatorname{id}$ for every $p\geq0$, and $h_0\delta_{-1}=\operatorname{id}$: the $i=0$ term is the identity and the terms $i>0$ are precisely the negatives of $\delta_{p-1}h_p$. Every horizontal stalk row is thus contracted, including its augmentation and every internal degree $q$; this uses functorial pullback on cohomology, not an acyclicity assumption about individual fibers or a global section of $f$. Step 4.1 (conclusion). The horizontal spectral sequence of the augmented cone has zero next page at every stalk by Step 3.1; its filtration is finite in each total degree by Step 1.1, so [F3] gives zero stalk cohomology of the cone. A complex of sheaves with all cohomology stalks zero is acyclic, proving the asserted quasi-isomorphism. All algebraic base changes of $f$ remain proper surjective and the same base-change identifications prove the pulled-back assertion without choosing compatible points; naturality of the augmentation follows from its units and face maps. Applying derived global sections to the supplied finite-diagonal total model gives the global statement. AC is inherited exactly through [A1].

projection.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice as inherited from the supplied six-functor resolutions. Let $X_\bullet\to X$ be an augmented simplicial finite-type complex algebraic variety ([[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]], [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]]). Assume $X_0\to X$ is proper surjective and, for each $p>0$, $X_p\to(\operatorname{cosk}_{p-1}\operatorname{sk}_{p-1}X_\bullet)_p$ is proper surjective over $X$, where skeleton and coskeleton are the standard finite-limit constructions of the simplicial category and the target is the matching object. Such an object is a proper hypercover; no smoothness or fiber acyclicity is assumed. For $F\in D^b_c(X;k)$ over a field, and $a_p:X_p\to X$, the augmentation gives $$F\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}Ra_{p*}a_p^*F,\qquad R\Gamma(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}_{p\geq0}R\Gamma(X_p,a_p^*F).$$ There is a natural strongly convergent spectral sequence $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X_p,a_p^*F)\Rightarrow H^{p+q}(X,F)$. If $F$ has cochain lower bound $a$, every diagonal $p+q=m$ is finite; degree $m$ and its differential are determined by levels through $p=m-a+1$. All proper-hypercover refinements induce the same comparison via the base object; any two such hypercovers have a proper common refinement. For $F=k_X$, $a=0$, this is the first-quadrant spectral sequence required for smooth-projective hyperresolutions.
projection.strategy: Assume AC as inherited from the supplied six-functor resolutions ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Sources: Dugger-Hollander-Isaksen Appendix A Proposition A.4, Lemma A.5 and Corollaries A.7-A.9 (bounded-hypercover bisimplicial Cech and retract argument; PDF pp. 35-38, read in full) and Stacks Project, Hypercoverings, Lemmas 4.2-4.5 and 5.1-5.3 (PDF pp. 5-10, read in full). [F1] [[lem-proper-surjective-maps-have-cohomological-descent-for-constructible-field-sheaves]] proves actual proper Cech descent, including arbitrary base change for bounded constructible coefficient complexes over any field. [F2] [[lem-bicosimplicial-derived-total-complex-agrees-with-diagonal-totalization]] supplies the natural alternating-face diagonal/double-total homotopy equivalence. [F3] [[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]] and [[lem-analytic-constructible-sheaves-admit-coherent-six-operations]] supply the ordinary coherent operations on bounded algebraically constructible complexes ([[def-algebraically-constructible-complex-of-analytic-field-sheaves]]), while [[lem-locally-split-cech-nerves-give-derived-cartesian-sheaf-descent]] supplies functorial coherent derived diagrams, strict simplicial resolutions, right-derived composition and their uniformly bounded-below total model; [[def-analytic-topology-and-finite-smooth-algebraic-stratifications]] fixes the analytic topology of the varieties. [F4] [[thm-bounded-filtered-complex-spectral-sequence-abuts-to-filtered-homology]] gives convergence for degreewise finite filtrations. [A1] AC is inherited only through the resolution inputs and [F1]; the finite coskeleton, product and retract constructions below make no new arbitrary selections. The proof reconstructs the matching-map vocabulary of [[def-simplicial-object-and-simplicial-commutative-ring]] inline: for the augmented simplicial variety $X_\bullet\to X$, $\operatorname{sk}_{p-1}$ is the simplicial truncation and $\operatorname{cosk}_{p-1}$ its right adjoint, formed by the finite limit formulas, and the matching object at level $p$ is $M_p=\lim_{[p]\to[k],k<p}X_k$. Step 1.1 (height zero). Let $U\to X$ be a bounded proper hypercover of height zero, that is $U=\operatorname{cosk}_0U_0$; this is the Cech nerve of the proper surjection $U_0\to X$, so [F1] proves both the sheaf and global augmentations. Suppose inductively they are proved for all bounded heights at most $n$, and let $U=\operatorname{cosk}_{n+1}U$ have height $n+1$. Put $V=\operatorname{cosk}_nU$: it is a proper hypercover of height at most $n$, since its original matching maps through degree $n$ are unchanged and its later matching maps are isomorphisms, so the inductive hypothesis applies to $V$. Step 2.1 (levelwise proper surjectivity). For every $j$, $U_j\to V_j$ is proper surjective. For $j\leq n$ it is the identity; in higher degree it is the map $\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{sk}_{n+1}\Delta[j],U)\to\operatorname{Hom}(\operatorname{sk}_n\Delta[j],U)$ between finite matching limits, and attaching the finitely many nondegenerate $(n+1)$-faces of $\Delta[j]$ to its $n$-skeleton makes it a Cartesian pullback of the finite product of the matching map $U_{n+1}\to M_{n+1}U$. A finite product over $X$ of proper surjections and any base change thereof is proper surjective; no local sections are required. Step 3.1 (bisimplicial Cech model). Form $W_{r,j}=U_j\times_{V_j}\cdots\times_{V_j}U_j$ with $r+1$ factors, horizontally the Cech nerve of $U_j\to V_j$, and pull coefficients from $X$ throughout. By [F1] and Step 2.1 every horizontally augmented derived row computes the coefficient complex on $V_j$, before and after pushing to $X$, so the induced augmentation into the double total is a quasi-isomorphism: apply [F4] to the triple-complex model of [F3], whose degrees $r,j\geq0$, $q\geq a$ have finite total diagonals. The inductive augmentation for $V$ then gives $F\simeq\operatorname{Tot}_{r,j}Ra_{W_{r,j}*}F_{W_{r,j}}$ and the analogous global statement; by [F2] this double total is naturally equivalent to the total on the diagonal $D_j=W_{j,j}$. Step 4.1 (retract over $X$). The bounded hypercover $U$ is a retract over $X$ of $D$: the map $i:U\to D$ repeats the same $U_j$ point in all $j+1$ horizontal factors, and through degree $n$ the map $U_j\to V_j$ is the identity, so $D_j=U_j$ there; in degree $n+1$ choose the first projection $D_{n+1}\to U_{n+1}$, whose faces and degeneracies agree with the degree-$\leq n$ identity maps because every horizontal factor has the same image in $V$ and those lower-degree maps are identities. This defines a map of $(n+1)$-truncations, and the universal property $U=\operatorname{cosk}_{n+1}U$ extends it uniquely to $r:D\to U$; the composite $ri$ is the identity through degree $n+1$, hence in every degree by the same universal property. Coefficient pullback reverses these maps, so the augmented total for $U$ is a retract of the augmented total for $D$, and a retract of an acyclic cone is acyclic. This completes the bounded-height induction. Step 5.1 (arbitrary height by truncation). For an arbitrary proper hypercover $U$, its $N$-coskeleton $U^{(N)}=\operatorname{cosk}_N\operatorname{sk}_NU$ is a bounded proper hypercover, so Step 4.1 applies to it; the map $U\to U^{(N)}$ is the identity through simplicial degree $N$. In the strict derived total model every internal degree is at least $a$, so total degrees $m-1,m,m+1$ use only simplicial degrees at most $m-a+1$. Choosing $N\geq\max(0,m-a+1)$ makes the totals for $U$ and $U^{(N)}$ have the same objects and differentials in these three degrees, hence the same degree-$m$ cohomology and the same augmentation maps; since this holds for every $m$, the augmentation for $U$ is a quasi-isomorphism. This is a finite-degree truncation argument, not an interchange of stalks or cohomology with an unjustified infinite product. Step 6.1 (spectral sequence and convergence). Filter the global total by simplicial degree. Its first page is $E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X_p,a_p^*F)$ with alternating pullback by faces as first differential. In degree $m$ its filtration has only $0\leq p\leq m-a$ nonzero pieces, so [F4] identifies the stationary page with the finite associated graded of $H^m(X,F)$, proving strong convergence; no finite-dimensionality of the individual $H^q$ groups is needed. Step 7.1 (refinements and constant coefficients). For two proper hypercovers $U,V$ over $X$, their levelwise product $R_j=U_j\times_XV_j$ is a common proper hypercover: finite matching limits commute with products, so each matching map of $R$ is the product over $X$ of the matching maps of $U$ and $V$ and is proper surjective, and its projections give the two refinements. By Step 5.1 both augmentations identify their totals with the same coefficient complex on $X$, so the comparison maps coincide after those identifications. A smooth-projective refinement is a separate supplied construction: the product of smooth maps over singular $X$ need not be smooth. For $F=k_X$ the lower bound is $a=0$ and the page is exactly the stated first-quadrant spectral sequence. AC is inherited precisely through [A1].
projection.axiom_use: AC is assumed and inherited from the resolution/six-functor suppliers and from [[lem-proper-surjective-maps-have-cohomological-descent-for-constructible-field-sheaves]]; the finite coskeleton, matching-product and retract constructions add no new arbitrary choices.
